blocks.p: An Arabic and English app for checking suspicious messages and choosing a safer next step.

Fatima Alhallak
Abdelfattah Sayed
Abdalrahman Moataz

Abu Dhabi Police x 42 Abu Dhabi hackathon
24 November 2026

TAAKAD addresses a familiar decision: a person receives an alarming message and is unsure whether to click, pay, share a code or approve a request. The MVP accepts a screenshot, pasted message or link, explains warning signs in Arabic or English and recommends a next action. It also offers guided recovery, official UAE awareness updates, learning material and structured community reports.

The interface is designed for the general public, including older users. Large controls, short steps, optional detail and language-aware layouts reduce the amount of technical information required to complete a check. The app is a prototype, not an official police service.

blocks.p: The weights above were supplied by the team after the kickoff presentation. They guide the organization of this report and do not represent a self-awarded score. Current software checks establish functioning behavior. Representative detection accuracy remains to be measured.

The home screen offers two large actions: Add a screenshot and Paste Text. For a photo, the user selects the image once, optionally crops it in the local preview, then taps Scan photo. Skipping crop keeps the complete image. Neither selecting nor cropping sends the image to OpenAI.

blocks.caption: Current English and Arabic crop previews using synthetic content. The same selected image is edited locally.

blocks.p: After Scan, the backend reads the visible message and sender. Clear readings move directly to relevant context questions. Unclear readings require correction, and extracted text remains editable before assessment. Questions such as whether the user has an account add unverified context; they do not authenticate the sender.

Final consent authorizes a text assessment. Changing a crop discards prior transcription, answers and consent so the edited image is read again. The interface preserves a recovery route when a request fails or is cancelled.

The supplied banking storyboard shows urgency and a request to verify an account. The caller storyboard shows a person claiming to represent a government department and asking for a UAE PASS approval. These are illustrative scenarios, not records of actual incidents. TAAKAD teaches users to verify independently and never approve an unexpected identity request.

Arabic and English are supported throughout the UI, with mirrored reading order, appropriately aligned text and both light and dark themes. The team confirmed the browser and crop journey in manual iPhone testing. Comprehension with older users and assistive technology still needs a dedicated study.

The product combines a screenshot-first check, limited context questions, an understandable result and relevant recovery guidance. Optional technical evidence stays behind More details. The proposed innovation lies in this connected, localized workflow built around an existing pretrained model.

Alerts use only approved Abu Dhabi Media Office RSS endpoints, subject to publisher guidance, robots checks and bounded collection. They preserve attribution, publication dates, source links and stale-content labels. The current integration covers one publisher. It does not scrape social media, commercial news outlets or arbitrary article pages. [1]

Official help is user initiated. Aman distinguishes security information from formal criminal reports, and its FAQ directs emergencies to 999. The app does not imply that publishing a community report creates a police case or triggers a callback. [2]

A screenshot is cropped locally, resized if necessary and encoded for external transcription. The backend returns the visible text and sender. Assessment then uses text, sender and relevant context rather than sending the original image again. Pasted text uses the assessment stage directly.

blocks.p: The backend validates field types, score/status consistency and bounded output. An assessed response requires an integer from 1 to 5. Insufficient information requires no numeric level. Severe requests for codes, payments or personal information can be dangerous without a link; the absence of a URL never caps the warning level.

The prompt treats submitted text, sender labels, links and context as untrusted data. Context answers are not proof of genuine identity. A reported exact-hostname match can raise the overall warning to at least 4 while preserving the separate message-only level. Reports may be wrong or old. [3, 4]

A single app request now handles recoverable network, provider and invalid-response failures with at most three attempts inside one 42-second budget. Billing, credential errors and explicit refusals are not retried. Exhausted attempts return an error, not an invented assessment.

No representative held-out detection benchmark has been completed. The 93 backend/helper tests and 78 browser tests check software behavior, validation and journeys. They do not establish a percentage accuracy, scam recall, false-positive rate or reduction in financial loss.

Begin with a proposed 200 labelled cases balanced between Arabic and English, plus a separate 40-case ambiguous set. Include realistic SMS and WhatsApp text/screenshots, written caller descriptions, no-link OTP/payment scams, impersonation, and legitimate banking, delivery and account messages. These are planning targets, not collected results.

Use permissioned or de-identified material. Two reviewers label each case independently, resolve disagreements and record the rationale. Split by message template and scam family to reduce leakage. Tune only on development cases, then freeze the prompt, model, UI thresholds and test set. Evaluate both the clean text and screenshot path so transcription failures are visible.

blocks.p: Report caution at level 2+ and high warning at level 4+, matching the current interface. Publish the confusion matrices, sample counts, uncertainty intervals and error examples. Reassurance must remain cautious even if future test performance is strong.

Results put a plain-language warning and the most useful next action first. Color is accompanied by a distinct symbol, a written label and an ordinal score. The number expresses warning signs, not the probability that a scam is present. Insufficient information has no numeric score.

blocks.caption: Current UI with real model responses to synthetic inputs. The two language examples are not an accuracy benchmark.

blocks.p: More details holds relevant quotes, additional actions, visible-link findings, source status and limitations. Quotes must occur in the submitted message or sender label. These are observable evidence and explanations, not a disclosure of the model's internal reasoning.

The recovery journey asks one question at a time about passwords, codes, payments, card details and opened links, then shows only relevant steps. Instructions preserve evidence before reporting or deleting. Completion ticks do not prove that an account is secure or money can be recovered.

The main prevention opportunity is before the user acts. TAAKAD provides a deliberate pause: choose the suspicious content, inspect warning signs and verify independently. After an incident, guided recovery supports the next decision. The project has not measured time saved, losses avoided or population-level impact.

blocks.p: The collector refreshes approved feeds while the backend runs, ordinarily hourly. Failed collection can use labelled cache for a bounded period of up to 24 hours. Stale, older, empty and unavailable content remain distinguishable. Topic filters are optional local preferences and can miss relevant items.

Learn contains four Arabic/English illustrated guides. The team's supplied UnknownCallerVideo and UnknownLinkVideo are exact 30-second MP4 copies with original audio. They play locally without autoplay and pause when leaving Learn. English videos are labelled honestly in both interfaces, with related Arabic/English written tips rather than a claim to provide translated audio or captions.

blocks.p: The browser reaches the backend through the app server's /api proxy. The backend binds to localhost on port 8787; the browser/app server uses port 8081. The local pairing token is available in the development bundle and is not production user authentication. Privileged moderator/support tokens and the OpenAI key stay outside the public source and client bundle.

GPT-4.1 mini was selected as a practical image/text and structured-output option, not a demonstrated best model. The team has not trained or fine-tuned model weights. Schema-constrained output reduces formatting problems but does not guarantee factual correctness or accurate detection. [3]

A normal screenshot check makes two model calls: transcription, then text assessment. Pasted text uses one. Optional report moderation uses the generated public summary only. Recoverable failures may produce up to three attempts per structured call and add provider cost. Live use depends on available credit and internet access.

The committee route is a browser QR with no Expo account or installation. Published Expo Go previews remain account-restricted under Expo's policy. A signed native release, persistent service deployment and production operational review remain future work. [5]

blocks.p: Community uses three questions and a preview instead of open discussion. Guests can read public features but posting requires a demo phone-code session. No SMS is sent, no phone ownership is verified and UAE PASS remains unavailable. A guest draft stays in memory during sign-in. AI moderation assists rather than certifies safety.

Report/session state is temporary and bounded, including expiry within one hour and loss on backend restart. Private own-report access is tied to the creating session, not recovery by an unverified phone number. Evidence uploads are not implemented. OS/browser caches can outlive the app's temporary state.

No receiving authority or referral agreement exists. The support handoff remains clearly labelled demonstration-only and separate consent is required even for demo access. Official contact options are alternatives, not evidence that a post creates a criminal complaint. Aman distinguishes information from formal reports. [2]

Production deployment requires HTTPS, real identity, durable access-controlled storage, audited retention/deletion, shared abuse protection and a reviewed authority workflow. The current trusted-LAN setup is for synthetic demonstrations, not a claim of production security or legal certification.

blocks.p: Use Node.js 22.18 or later. From the complete repository, install locked dependencies and generate local setup. Put an available OpenAI key only in the private server/.env file. Never put a secret in chat, the repository or the presentation.

blocks.code:
npm ci
npm run setup
npm run demo

blocks.p: On Windows use npm.cmd if PowerShell restricts npm.ps1. The demo command starts or reuses the matching backend/app session and shows a browser QR. Scan with the phone Camera and open Safari/Chrome. No Expo login is required. Keep the laptop awake, the server running and both devices on the same trusted Wi-Fi with peer traffic allowed.

The public repository contains the complete MVP, dependency lockfile, safe environment example, assets, tests, source notices and README on master. Provider outages or exhausted credit can still prevent a live result. The earlier intermittent error was not captured exactly; bounded recovery was verified with injected transient failures and strict validation.

First, complete the held-out bilingual accuracy study and publish false-warning, false-reassurance and abstention results. Second, test comprehension and completion of safety actions with older users, including accessibility and Android/native interruptions. Third, add real identity, secure persistence and operational controls before public deployment. Finally, agree a receiving organization and formal consent/delivery process before enabling real support referrals.

Notifications, widgets, live call/message interception, voice cloning/TTS, real SMS, UAE PASS integration and authority case delivery are outside the current MVP. The user-supplied storyboards illustrate risks; they are not evidence of actual events or guaranteed outcomes. The team remains responsible for participation eligibility, media rights, final portal uploads and the required recorded one-minute non-AI-generated submission demo.
